note.note:
Subjective:
- Presenting complaint and trigger/exposure:
  • Severe left-sided headache beginning around midday today.  
  • No identified food, drug, or environmental trigger.

- Symptom timeline and progression:
  • Preceded by visual aura (“zig-zag lines,” blurred vision) a few minutes before pain onset.  
  • Throbbing pain worsens with head/neck movement or leaning forward.  
  • Two episodes of vomiting since onset.  
  • Similar episode a few weeks ago that lasted “a couple of days.”

- ENT symptoms:
  • Throat swelling/closure sensation: none.  
  • Voice change/hoarseness: none.  
  • Dysphagia/odynophagia: none.  
  • Drooling: none.  
  • Nasal/ocular: photophobia reported; no nasal congestion/itching, no tearing.  
  • Stridor/noisy breathing: none.  
  • Dyspnea: denied.  
  • Swelling lips/tongue/uvula/face: none.  
  • Ear pain/hearing change: none.  
  • Neck pain/swelling: headache worsens with movement; no focal neck swelling reported.

- Relevant past episodes and treatments:
  • Similar headache several weeks ago; self-treated with rest and over-the-counter analgesics.  
  • No prior ED visits, hospitalizations, or injection therapy for headaches.

- Allergies and current medications:
  • Drug/food/environmental allergies: none stated.  
  • Medications: Microgynon oral contraceptive (dose/route/frequency not documented).  
  • No rescue medications (e.g., triptans) on hand.

- Social context:
  • Lives alone; works in fashion industry under significant job stress.  
  • No smoking or alcohol use.

Objective:
- Observable swelling/distribution: not reported.  
- Airway/breathing: patient denies breathlessness; no stridor noted.  
- Mental status: alert, oriented, expresses anxiety about possible serious disease.  
- Vitals/exam: Not recorded (telephone consultation).  
- Presence of another person: none; patient alone.

Assessment:
- Probable migraine without overt ENT or allergic features.  
  • Justification: unilateral throbbing headache, visual aura, photophobia, nausea/vomiting, prior similar episode, no focal neurological deficits, no airway or facial swelling.

Plan:
- Immediate actions/advice:
  • Trial of analgesia: acetaminophen or co-codamol; consider NSAID (ibuprofen or naproxen) if tolerated (dose/route/frequency not documented).  
  • Begin headache diary to identify triggers and frequency.

- Patient instructions:
  • Seek urgent care if headache worsens, fails to improve within 2–3 days, or if new symptoms develop (weakness, visual change, worsening neck pain, speech difficulty).

- Escalation criteria/red flags emphasized:
  • Sudden severe headache, persistent vomiting, neurological deficits, visual loss, confusion, or any airway/breathing difficulty.

- Follow-up:
  • Review in one week to reassess headache pattern and discuss possible prophylactic therapy if episodes persist.  
  • No ENT/allergy referral indicated at present.

Quality checks (document_quality):
● Missing but expected elements: objective vitals (BP, HR, RR, SpO₂, temperature); detailed neurological/ENT examination; confirmed allergy list; availability of migraine-specific rescue medication (e.g., triptan); assessment of auto-injector need not applicable but airway evaluation minimal.  
● Internal conflicts: none noted in transcript.  
● Transcript quality: clear audio; minor conversational overlaps but clinical content intelligible.
